item.title: TechAnim in Unreal: AnimInstance and AnimationBlueprint
TechAnim in Unreal: AnimNotify and AnimNotifyState
item.description:
Among the most powerful tools that Unreal Engine offers out-of-the-box are AnimNotifies and AnimNotifyStates. These two features allow us to execute any logic we might want at a specific point in an animation. That might be firing of VFX at the feet of our character each time they take a step, or playing an audio cue while they are charging up an attack, or something else entirely.

They are one of the most-used ways of having animation directly interface with the rest of the game and I can pretty much guarantee you that any Unreal Engine Project of quality uses them in some capacity. They are hugely flexible tools, for anyone touching animation assets, be that Animators, Tech-Artists, or Engineers, so knowing their ins and outs is key to creating great games and workflows.

item.title: On Good Blueprints
item.description:
From time to time, I am involved in discussions on whether it is possible to create “objectively good” Blueprints in Unreal Engine. The realistic answer is: Probably not. Not fully objectively at least. But that still doesn’t mean that I don’t have some strong opinions on how Blueprints should look, so here we are.

My philosophy of what makes Blueprints “good” is a result of about 8 years of using the visual programming language, initially just on my own and in small non-professional teams, but since 2020 also in a more professional setting. This means that while I obviously don’t know how you do your Blueprints I have seen a bunch of people (including myself of course) making very good and very bad decisions when creating these graphs.
